headline: Metabolism converts food into usable energy—your body is a controlled combustion engine
universal_truth: Transformation requires work; raw inputs must be processed before they become usable
fun_facts: Your body produces enough heat to boil half a gallon of water per hour
The brain uses 20% of your body's energy despite being only 2% of your weight
ATP—the energy currency of cells—is produced and consumed so fast that you cycle through your body weight in ATP daily
discussion_questions: What inputs do you transform into outputs?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You're burning right now. Slowly, controlled, but burning. Your cells break down food molecules, extract energy, and release carbon dioxide and water—just like fire. Metabolism is combustion in slow motion, turning fuel into power.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Food has energy, but you can't use it directly. Metabolism transforms raw fuel into usable power. What does this transformation process teach us?

options.text: Raw inputs aren't directly usable—transformation converts them into forms that can power specific processes; processing is always required
options.response: Yes. You can't run on bread directly—digestion and metabolism convert it to ATP, which powers muscles. Every useful output requires processing raw inputs.

options.text: Food just needs to be broken down smaller
options.response: Size matters, but the deeper change is converting chemical bonds into ATP—usable energy currency...

q1.title: Energy Currency
q1.script: Cells use ATP as energy currency. Metabolism converts food into ATP, which powers everything: muscle contraction, thought, growth. Like cash from goods, ATP is the universal energy medium.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Energy Currency"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Efficiency and Waste
q2.script: No conversion is perfectly efficient. Some energy escapes as heat—that's why you're warm. About 40% of food energy becomes ATP; the rest becomes heat. Inefficiency is thermodynamically inevitable.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Metabolic Rate
q3.script: Your metabolic rate determines how fast you burn fuel. It varies with activity, size, age, and health. Managing energy means matching input to output—eat for the metabolism you have.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Transformation requires work. Raw inputs must be processed before they become usable. Every output requires processing.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 242. Tomorrow, we'll explore blood's endless journey—circulation. Until then, notice your body's metabolism at work.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Transformation Audit - What Do You Convert?
growTrack.activity: What raw inputs do you receive—information, resources, opportunities? What do you transform them into? Every person is a metabolic system, converting inputs to outputs. How efficient is your personal metabolism?
